newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - July 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - July 31.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Foster's Brewing Group has come under pressure from the Molson group of companies of Canada to abandon its A$1 billion stake in Molson Breweries. The two groups each own 40 percent of Molson Breweries and the Molson Group wants to increase its share to 100 percent. Page 19.

BHP is poised to expand into the world nickel market with a decision expected soon on its US$1.2 billion development of its Gag Island nickel deposit in Indonesia. BHP has invested over A$22 million on a drilling programme as part of a feasibility study, soon to be finalised. Page 19.

Savage Resources Ltd managing director Jim Wall resigned yesterday following conflict with the company's board over the future direction of the firm. Wall said yesterday his aggressive business approach was at odds with the board's preferred option of developing existing assets. Page 20.

Banking sources confirmed yesterday that North American company Barrick Gold Corp had purchased about A$500 million. The move has increased speculation that Barrick Gold Corp will soon launch a take-over bid for Great Central Mines NL valued at A$800 million. Page 20.

An extraordinary general meeting of Hyal Pharmaceutical Ltd yesterday saw two independent directors voted off the board by the Canadian parent Hyal Pharmaceutical Corp. Former directors John Leaper and Peter Simpson plan legal acion over the meeting which they believe was invalid. Page 22.

The Austrim group yesterday moved to complete its take-over of Hawker Richardson with shareholders endorsing a final offer of A$1.86 per share. Austrim chairman Alan Jackson said that now the company had a majority holding in Hawker it would aim for a compulsory acquisition. Page 22.
THE AUSTRALIAN

The Australian Stock Exchange will relist shares in Aristocrat Leisure Industries after halting trading in the company's stock a week ago following the withdrawal of the company's poker machine distribution by the Colorado Gaming Control Commission in the United States. Aristocrat has launched a legal challenge to that action claiming that some allegations are incorrect and defamatory. Page 21.

Cigarette manufacturer WD & HO Wills has warned that its extraordinary 111 percent profit growth in the six months to June 30 is unlikely to continue. WD & HO Wills chief executive Stuart Watterton says the re-emergence of price discounting has created uncertainty in the market. Page 23.

A soon-to-be-released report, "The Global Information Economy - The Way Ahead", warns that the future competitiveness of business and industry will be dependent on effective use of information technology but Australia risks falling behind. The report is the product of a 10-month inquiry by a taskforce commissioned by Federal Industry Minister John Moore and chaired by Bond University's Professor Ashley Goldsworthy. Page 23.

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission said yesterday it had no further opposition to CSR and Mackay Refined Sugars merging their sugar operations. Following the announcement the two companies said they would end their price war which has gretly damaged the sugar industry. Page 23.

Newcrest Mining has posted annual gold production of less than 500,000 ounces with forward sales projecting an average realised price of A$700 an ounce for the next decade. The company has hedged production for the current financial year at A$580 an Ounce, an increase of its hedging position by 45 percent from 3.6 million ounces to 5.2 million ounces. Page 25.

Woodside Petroleum has reported a five percent rise in sales of LNG and domestic gase from A$231 million to A$242 million for the first half of the year, lifting earnings from its North-West Shelf project and domestic gas operations. Upgraded liquefied natural gas facilities have been credited with increasing the company's share of revenue from the A$12 billion North-West shelf project. Page 25.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Don Bourke has taken over from John David as chief executive of David's Ltd after the company announced plans for an abnormal writedown of $262 million. The group has been run by the David family for 70 years. Page 29.

Figures released yesterday show Australian consumers are placing their money into superannuation funds managed by life offices instead of buying medium and long-term life insurance and superannuation plans. The figures showed a 55 percent increase in fund inflows to managed super funds in 1996, with AMP currently leading the superannuation sales field. Page 31.

In a decision the company describes as restructuring, Grey Advertising general manager Scott Wagstaff has been made redundant 12 months after he joined the company. Grey managing director Barry Anderson said the advertising market was tough at the moment with clients not spending as much as they said they would. He described Wagstaff's redundancy as purely a restructuring move with his position as general manager becoming obsolete. Page 32.

GIO Australia has launched a new business, All-States Security Services, to provide security alarms for GIO customers in a bid to reduce insurance claim payouts and increase the company's profitability. The business will be known as GIO Security Services in the Australian Capital Territory and New South Wales. General manager David Smith said the company would target small businesses and home owners first. Page 33.

Paint maker Wattyl has increased its annual net profit by 27.1 percent to A$25.8 million for the year to June 30 after good returns from United States business initiatives in Australia. Wattyl's overall sales for the same period were A$494 million with anaging director Greg Boshell describing the Australian paint market as quiet with strong competition putting the pressure on profits. Page 33.

An independent report by Grant Samuel and Associates is believed to have described the proposed A$2.2 billion merger of QNI and South African mining giant Gencor as being not fair and reasonable. QNI shares were suspended from trading yesterday amid talk that Gencor was considering altering the terms of the proposal. Page 33.
THE AGE

The 13th of November has been established as the most likely date for the one-third float of Telstra, valued at about A$36 billion. Sources believe the government wants the sale finalised before investors start thinking about Christmas. It is also expected that Telstra employees will be offered one free share for every four they purchase up to a limit of 500 free shares. Page B1.

The Victorian Power Exchange has announced it is seeking tenders from generators to supply electricity during the sState's summer peaks in demand. The Victorian Power Exchange is responsible for monitoring the sState's electricity industry and believes the increase of air-conditioning units is partly to blame for the increased demand for electricity over summer. Page B2.

Delta Gold has announced the company is delaying its Gold Feather project in Western Australia due to the fall in the price of gold. Delta Gold chief operating officer Terry Burgess said the company would go ahead with the project when the price of gold improved. Delta Gold has also announced it will spend A$32 million on exploration this year with 60 percent to be spent in Australia and the remainder mostly in Zimbabwe. Page B2.

Telstra has announced a deal to licence the Melbourne designed Flexcab billing system to Telecom Argentina, in a move that could earn the company up to A$75 million and see 250 jobs created in Melbourne. Telstra has also said it will have another announcment to make shortly in regards to a substantial deal it has done with a United States telecommunications giant. Page B2.

Mining company Rio Tinto has reported good increases for its key commodities for the first half of 1997. Strong production figures and revenue from copper, iron ore, coal, aluminium and gold were the main contributors. Page B3.

Three of the automobile industry leaders and an auto consultant have outlined the future growth, development and job maintenance for Australia's car industry. The group said Australia can have a A$6 billion export future if companies and the goverment work to sustain productivity and increase overseas sales by breaking protected regional markets. Page B3.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
